Dangerous Goods

مؤشر الميل

A device attached to a shipment to detect and indicate if a package has been tilted beyond a preset angle during handling or transit.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is مؤشر الميل?

In this glossary, مؤشر الميل refers to: A device attached to a shipment to detect and indicate if a package has been tilted beyond a preset angle during handling or transit.

How is مؤشر الميل used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "مؤشر الميل إلزامي لجميع الشحنات التي تحتوي على مواد كيميائية مخبرية حساسة حسب سياسة البضائع الخطرة الخاصة بالناقل."

Who uses مؤشر الميل?

مؤشر الميل is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A device attached to a shipment to detect and indicate if a package has been tilted beyond a preset angle during handling or transit.

Operational example

A tilt indicator is mandatory for all shipments containing sensitive lab chemicals per the carrier’s hazardous goods policy.

Localized term
